title: FlashAttention-3
hook: FlashAttention-3 rewrote the attention kernel for Hopper GPUs — overlapping compute with the softmax and using FP8 to push attention close to the hardware's peak.
key_points: Third-generation exact-attention kernel, specialized for NVIDIA Hopper (H100) GPUs.
Overlaps matrix-multiply and softmax work and uses asynchrony to hide latency.
Adds FP8 low-precision support for even higher throughput.
Speeds up both training and inference of long-context transformers.
content_html: FlashAttention-3 is the third iteration of the exact-attention kernel that made long-context transformers practical. Where the original FlashAttention avoided materializing the full attention matrix to save memory, version 3 is hand-tuned for NVIDIA's Hopper architecture, squeezing far more of the GPU's theoretical throughput out of the same computation.
extra_html:
How it works

The kernel exploits Hopper-specific features: it overlaps the matrix multiplications with the softmax normalization so the GPU is never idle waiting on one stage, and it uses asynchronous memory operations to hide data-movement latency. It also supports FP8, an 8-bit floating-point format, trading a little precision for a large throughput gain. The result is attention that runs much closer to the hardware's peak performance.

Why it matters

Attention is the throughput bottleneck for long sequences, so kernel-level speedups translate directly into cheaper training and faster inference. FlashAttention-3 let labs train and serve longer-context models on the same hardware, and it is a clear illustration of the "hardware lottery" — the algorithms that win are often the ones that map best onto the chips we actually have.

related.title: The KV Cache & Continuous Batching
related.hook: Generating one token reuses every prior key and value - that growing cache is why LLM inference is memory-bound, and continuous batching is how servers fight back.

related.title: Multi-Query Attention: Faster Decoding
related.hook: Share one key/value head across all query heads - the KV cache shrinks by a factor of H and decoding gets dramatically faster with barely any quality cost.
